clue.text: Congratulatory gestures: give baked goods to Spooner

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two pieces exchange their first consonants

parts.note: give as a noun is slack, play in a rope
baps are soft bread rolls

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hand pastries to the famously muddled Dr Spooner by way of congratulations.
explanation.walkthrough: SLACK BAPS becomes BACK SLAPS once the first sounds swap. A bap is a British soft bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap on the back is a hearty gesture of praise or celebration, so these are congratulatory acts.

clue.text: Pack up book that might be mine

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a mob is a pack or crowd of people or animals

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to pack up a book that could be theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' reads as the possessive, but it is the explosive device sunk in the ground or sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine is an explosive device, a kind of bomb planted to detonate on contact.

clue.text: Attractive copper item uncovered

indicators.note: a word uncovered loses its outer letters, so only the middle of item is kept

parts.note: its two inner letters are used

explanation.surface: An appealing copper object is unearthed in an excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means pretty or appealing in a charming way, a near synonym of attractive.

clue.text: A fine father feeding child culinary plant

indicators.note: the first pieces are fed into the child, placed inside that word

parts.note: a son is a child
taken as written
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A good father nourishes his child with a cooking herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is the crocus whose stigmas are dried as a costly spice for cooking.

clue.text: Storyteller matures with release of good work

indicators.note: releasing the good means letting its letter go from the preceding word

parts.note: ages means grows older or matures
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A narrator grows older as a fine piece of writing is published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'release of good work' reads as publication, but release attaches only to good.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the ancient Greek author credited with the famous animal fables, a teller of stories.

clue.text: Pig tender when I dress cut and wound

indicators.note: wound as in twisted round, so the letters are wound into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing a final letter

parts.note: the word itself, shortened

explanation.surface: Someone who looks after pigs, when I bandage a cut and a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress cut and wound' looks like first aid; wound is the past tense of wind, not an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A swineherd is a person who keeps and looks after pigs, so a tender of them.

clue.text: Strokes of strong swimmers

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud or strong
eels are swimming fish

explanation.surface: The arm movements made by powerful swimmers in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strokes' suggests swimming strokes, but it is the verb: touches gently.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroke something is to touch it with the hand, which is what one does when one feels it.

clue.text: Prefers low-scoring cards, holding a five

indicators.note: the cards hold the next pieces inside them

parts.note: fours are cards of low value
taken as written
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A card player likes keeping cheap cards while holding a five.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour something is to like it better than the alternatives, the same as preferring it.

clue.text: Great attempt to consume US author's lengthy works

indicators.note: the pair eat the author, taking him inside, between the two words

parts.note: epic means great in scale
a try is an attempt
Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: A huge effort to devour an American writer's long books.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic poetry is long narrative verse such as the Iliad, extended works of heroic poetry.

clue.text: Starter of soup with bananas sure gains sweet quality

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: its first letter only

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dieter fears that soup to start, then bananas, surely piles on sweet weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' sounds like a menu course beside the soup, but means a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugariness is the state of being sugary, a sweet characteristic of taste.

clue.text: Apt decoration reflected theme

indicators.note: a reflection runs the letters back the other way

parts.note: fit means apt or suitable
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A suitable ornament mirrored the main idea of the design.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring idea or element in art or music, a theme.

clue.text: Working laboriously, runner struggling after second of events

parts.note: a ski is a runner, as on a sledge

indicators.note: only the second letter of the word is used

parts.note: its second letter only
vying means competing or struggling

explanation.surface: An athlete toiling hard after the second race of the meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete but is a ski; skivvying is doing menial drudgery, a skivvy being a British word for a lowly servant.
explanation.definitionFit: To skivvy is to do drudgery as a menial servant, labouring hard at chores.

clue.text: Sportsperson's tour with the French jersey

parts.note: a trip is a tour or journey
le is French for the
in Britain a jumper is a sweater, also called a jersey

explanation.surface: An athlete's journey, with the yellow jersey of the French tour in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Tour de France and its jersey; 's is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A triple jumper is an athlete in the hop, step and jump event.

clue.text: Botched up last curl of carving

indicators.note: something botched is messed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A craftsman ruined the final curl of a carving.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculptural means relating to sculpture, the art of carving or modelling forms.

clue.text: Support that man and girl in Wessex seeing soothsayer

parts.note: a prop is a support
he refers to that man
Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Hardy's heroine set in his fictional Wessex

explanation.surface: A countryman and a Wessex girl visit a fortune teller for help.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy set his novels in a fictional Wessex in southwest England; Tess is his best-known heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetess is a woman who foretells the future, a female seer.

clue.text: Wrongfully torch bridges in ancient city

indicators.note: the rearranged letters span the little word, holding it inside
done wrongly, so the letters are put in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arsonists unlawfully set fire to the bridges of an old Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torch bridges' reads as arson, but bridges is a verb here: straddles.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth was a powerful city-state of classical Greece, famed in antiquity.

clue.text: Sound of cat going between stores in direction of residence

indicators.note: the cat's cry goes into the middle of the stores

parts.note: hoards are stores or stockpiles
a mew is a cat's cry

explanation.surface: A cat heads off home, mewing past the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' looks like shops but means hoards.
explanation.definitionFit: Homewards means towards home, the place one lives.

clue.text: Space around plant native to Asia, perhaps

indicators.note: the space goes around the plant, enclosing it

parts.note: an en is a printer's space
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Room is left around a plant which may come from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's unit of space.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern describes things from the East, such as Asia, hence the perhaps signalling an example.

clue.text: It's locked in aboard

indicators.note: the letters are locked inside the word that follows

parts.note: the word contains the answer in its middle letters

explanation.surface: Something is securely fastened on board a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the answer is literally inside the word, and an oar sits in a rowlock aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is held in a rowlock on board a rowing boat, so it is locked in aboard.

clue.text: Regularly taken ale in pub; daily mass relief for chaps

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

parts.note: every other letter of these words, from the second
m is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A drinker takes ale at the pub and Mass daily as relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaps' looks like men, but means chapped skin, as on the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip balm is a salve that soothes chapped, cracked lips.

clue.text: Name of female figure in Sicilian mount climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading from bottom to top
the figure goes inside the mountain's name

parts.note: Etna is the volcano on Sicily
ten is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: A woman's statue is found by climbers on a Sicilian volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female figure' reads as a statue, but the figure is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Annette is a woman's given name, a diminutive of Anne.

clue.text: Picked up sweets and leaves

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio, heard rather than seen

parts.note: desserts are sweet courses, called sweets in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone collected candy and fallen foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a sweet is a pudding course, a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to leave or abandon, so deserts means leaves.

clue.text: Group scoffing aromatic confectionery

indicators.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, so the group takes the herb inside

parts.note: a set is a group
a herb is an aromatic plant

explanation.surface: A crowd wolfs down fragrant sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain sherbet is a fizzy sweet powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet is a sugary effervescent powder sold as a sweet, so a confection.

clue.text: Fairy tale adapted: hot news piece

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the queen is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A fairy story is reworked into a breaking news item.
explanation.definitionFit: The Snow Queen is Hans Christian Andersen's well-known fairy story.

clue.text: Pundit trashing wingers with Germany nullified

indicators.note: throwing out the word's wings, its outer letters

parts.note: only its inner letters are kept
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A football pundit rubbishes the wide players after Germany's goal is disallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wingers' sounds like footballers, but means the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo something is to reverse or cancel it, so undid means nullified.

clue.text: Worthless person about to enter Australia from south

indicators.note: in a down entry, read from the south means bottom to top
the short word goes into Australia's nickname

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A useless individual is about to arrive in Australia from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A zero is a nonentity, someone of no importance.

clue.text: Workers ignoring Ts and Cs in BTEC test

indicators.note: ignoring the letters means leaving them out of the text

parts.note: the word itself, losing its T and its C
the word itself, losing both its Ts

explanation.surface: Employees skip the terms and conditions in a vocational exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ts and Cs' looks like terms and conditions, but means the letters T and C. A BTEC is a British vocational qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker bees are the sterile females of the hive, so bees are crossword workers.

clue.text: Once more went in grass concealing key

indicators.note: the grass hides the key inside itself

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
Enter is a key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A key was hidden in the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter is to come back in, going in a second time.

clue.text: Note first of boyfriends always returning

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

parts.note: its first letter only

indicators.note: going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A short message from the first boyfriend who keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a musical note lasting two semibreves.

clue.text: Large passage in shop out of a type of thread

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: out of here means without, so the letter a is taken away from the passage

parts.note: an aisle is a walkway between the shelves of a shop
the letter a, which is removed

explanation.surface: A wide shop aisle has run out of a certain kind of thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' reads as 'sold out of' in the surface, but it means minus: take A from AISLE to leave ISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth, tightly twisted cotton yarn, once used for stockings.

clue.text: Being subversive, small amendment added to promissory notes

parts.note: an edit is an amendment
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A small change is made to some written promises to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Seditious means inciting rebellion against authority, the same as subversive.
